note: custom_field_graphql exposes Custom Field (`custom`) fields and their subfield columns through GraphQL Compose. It registers GraphQL Compose FieldType/SchemaType plugins and extends graphql_compose.settings field_config.<entity>.<bundle>.<field> with a `subfields` map (custom_field_graphql.subfield.* = {enabled: bool, name_sdl: string}). IMPORTANT GROUNDING CAVEAT: this benchmark site does NOT have the graphql_compose project installed (and `composer require` is out of scope for this campaign), so the submodule itself cannot be enabled here. The easy (recipe) cases are fully valid text questions. The medium/hard cases are grounded in the module's real config contract — the `subfields` structure inside graphql_compose.settings — and their setup/reset/verify scripts round-trip that config object; they were smoke-tested at the config level, but a full end-to-end GraphQL query check requires graphql_compose to be installed. The scripts mutate ONLY the graphql_compose.settings config object under a namespaced field path and restore it, touching no other module.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal submodule custom_field_graphql do, and which contrib project must be installed for it to work?
evals.expected_output: It integrates the Custom Field module with GraphQL Compose, exposing `custom` fields and their subfield columns in a GraphQL schema. It depends on the graphql_compose project.

evals.prompt: In custom_field_graphql, how can each column (subfield) of a Custom Field be individually controlled in the GraphQL schema, and what are the two per-subfield settings?
evals.expected_output: It adds a `subfields` map to the GraphQL Compose field settings (graphql_compose.settings field_config.*), keyed by column machine name, with two settings per column: `enabled` (include in schema) and `name_sdl` (the GraphQL schema field name, used to give underscored machine names a clean SDL name).

evals.prompt: Why does custom_field_graphql provide a `name_sdl` setting for a Custom Field column, and what is its default?
evals.expected_output: name_sdl sets the GraphQL/SDL field name a column is exposed as; it defaults to the column machine name. It exists because Custom Field column machine names often contain underscores that are not ideal GraphQL identifiers, so you can expose e.g. price_amount as priceAmount.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a Custom Field's GraphQL Compose settings have one column renamed for the schema. Inspect the graphql_compose.settings configuration for field_config.node.cfgql_eval.field_cfgql and report the GraphQL schema field name (name_sdl) configured for the 'price_amount' subfield.

On this Drupal site, one subfield of a Custom Field has been excluded from the GraphQL schema. Inspect graphql_compose.settings field_config.node.cfgql_eval.field_cfgql and report which subfield has enabled = false.

On this Drupal site, in the GraphQL Compose settings for the Custom Field at field_config.node.cfgql_eval.field_cfgql, expose the 'price_amount' column in the GraphQL schema under the clean name 'priceAmount' (set its subfield name_sdl). Apply the change to the live configuration.

On this Drupal site, in the GraphQL Compose settings for the Custom Field at field_config.node.cfgql_eval.field_cfgql, exclude the 'secret_note' column from the GraphQL schema (disable that subfield). Apply the change to the live configuration.
